A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GCD/P-GCD research work. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original xLAM, CommonGen, and Spider evaluations, alongside runtime measurements, HMM-size sensitivity results, and automaton-size comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark evaluations and supplementary computational analyses.

M1.justification: Section 2 corrects the documented SMC reweighting step from whole-prefix importance weights to incremental weights for per-step resampling. Algorithm 1 replaces its final diagonal-of-matrix-product computation with an equivalent elementwise product and summation. The GCD/P-GCD constructions remain unchanged; these revisions do not establish that implementations changed or experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate xLAM function calling in JSON and Python-like formats, CommonGen keyword-constrained generation, and Spider text-to-SQL. The automaton-size scenarios are also retained; no dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within the corresponding experiments, including the rejection-sampling reference, LCD/SMC comparisons, and unconstrained-generation latency baseline. The expanded discussion of Ctrl-G does not introduce an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The reported splits, sample counts, metrics, particle budgets, and testing procedures are retained. Newly stated token budgets and explicit Spider model settings supply previously missing details; the PDFs do not establish changes to the experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The HMM-size sensitivity study in Table 3, runtime analysis in Table 2, and NFA/DFA case studies in Figure 4 and Table 5 are retained. No new ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is introduced.

E5.justification: Table 2 reports the same means and standard deviations over three seeds in both versions. The plotted uncertainty bands are also unchanged, with no added run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The numerical entries in Tables 1–5 and plotted results in Figures 2–4 are unchanged. For example, Table 4 retains Spider accuracy of 59.8% for LCD and 56.2% for P-GCD at one particle. Table 2's caption now says milliseconds, matching its already-existing ms/token header rather than changing the measurements.

T1.justification: Section 2 replaces phi(x1:t)/q(x1:t) with phi(x1:t)/[phi(x1:t-1)q(xt|x<t)] and defines the empty-prefix potential as one. Appendix A corrects the attribution of the biased probabilities to q_lcd rather than the target conditional distribution. The automaton/HMM definitions, Theorems 4.3–4.4, and Appendix B remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: tensorized automata for budget-aware constraint satisfaction, HMM-based probabilistic guidance, and faster SMC convergence than LCD-based proposals. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 explicitly qualifies that the product distribution equals the constrained HMM distribution for DFAs, while NFAs introduce accepting-path weighting that SMC proposal correction can accommodate. Section 5.4 now limits the Spider advantage to k >= 4 and explains the poorer one-particle P-GCD result through the absence of resampling correction.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies token budgets of 128 for both xLAM formats, 32 for CommonGen, and 128 for Spider. It also explicitly identifies Spider's Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct base model and 1,024-state HMM. These improve documentation of existing experiments; hardware, training-time information, and the code-access statement are retained.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds an explicit contrast with Ctrl-G covering NFA support, SMC sampling, and tensorized GPU implementation. The cited-work set is unchanged; publication-year, venue, title, and author-name corrections update existing references.

P1.justification: There are localized prose revisions and explanatory additions in the SMC setup, experimental discussion, related work, and Appendix A, plus grammar and bibliography cleanup. The main section sequence and appendix organization are preserved.

P2.justification: Figure 2 drops the percentage designation from its caption, Table 1 identifies xLAM explicitly, and Table 2 corrects its caption's latency unit. Figure 4 moves from page 8 to page 9, accompanied by table and text reflow. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 improves technical correctness through the SMC-weight correction and Appendix A's distribution labeling, documents missing experimental settings, and more accurately explains NFA guidance and Spider's one-particle weakness. Caption corrections also remove ambiguity. These are useful, focused gains in correctness, reproducibility, and interpretation; the empirical evidence and central contributions remain unchanged.
